newsitem.title: USA: S. Korea, N. Korea, U.S. agree on talks.
newsitem.headline: S. Korea, N. Korea, U.S. agree on talks.

text.p: The United States, South Korea and North Korea agreed on Monday to hold four-nation talks in New York on Aug. 5 to discuss replacing the armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War with a formal treaty.
A joint statement by the three countries after a day-long senior-level meeting in New York said China would join the August talks.
The meeting will determine details to prepare for the formal start of four-party peace talks, according to a separate statement by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.
"The three delegations agreed that the four parties involved will meet for preparatory talks on Aug. 5 in New York," Albright's statement said.
"At that meeting, the four parties will decide the date, venue, agenda and procedures for the formal start of four-party peace talks," it said.

The proposed four-party negotiations would aim to replace the armistice with a formal peace treaty. The armistice ended the fighting in the Korean War but technically not the war on the Korean peninsula.
